findings.label: Empty-mesh fallback is scale-times too large
findings.detail: RobustLocalBounds returns a local size of 1 for a zero-vertex mesh and FitBoxToMesh assigns it straight to box.size, which is a 230 m collider on a blocker and 255 m on a table; the old code divided a 1 m world fallback by scale and produced a 1 m box. Unreachable for the 33 props in this scene. Fix: treat an empty mesh as not knockable (FitBoxToMesh reports failure, MakeKnockable counts it as noMesh).

findings.label: Refusals never reach the headline
findings.detail: The headline StringBuilder never mentions the unseated list and the severity ladder is suspect -> not-saved -> oversized -> Debug.Log, so a bake in which every prop was refused still opens with '33 props made knockable... Scene saved' at info level. Fix: append the unseated count to the headline and promote it to a warning when unseated.Count > 0.

findings.label: Undo not recorded on the reference-box re-fit
findings.detail: On the already-knockable path the measured branch guards its mutation with Undo.RecordObject(oldBox, "refit box") but the ApplyReferenceBox branch beside it records nothing, so Ctrl+Z after a re-bake restores a table's box and leaves a blocker's copied box in place. Inherited from the old code, newly inconsistent with its sibling branch. Fix: add the matching Undo.RecordObject.

findings.label: Blockers start 8.6 cm inside the road
findings.detail: ReferenceClearance yields -0.086 m for the RoadBlocker04 family, which is what puts .001 and .003 at exactly the hand-placed .002's y = 0.400. The bodies are baked asleep, so the overlap is resolved as a depenetration pop at up to Unity's default 10 m/s on first contact. Deliberate trade documented in the plan. Fix if it shows in playtest: rb.maxDepenetrationVelocity around 1 m/s keeps the exact y match, or clamp the gap to Mathf.Max(0f, gap) and lose it.

findings.label: Lift cap is near-inert and proportional
findings.detail: The ray starts at boxTop + 0.25 m, which already bounds any achievable lift at about the box's own height, so max(1 m, box height) only rejects inside a 25 cm window. The cap also scales with the prop and permits a 5.36 m lift for picnictable02. The overhang protection is the ray start, not the cap; do not loosen the ray start on the assumption the cap covers it.

findings.label: Deeply sunk props can no longer be recovered
findings.detail: A prop more than its own box height plus 25 cm below the surface starts its ray below the ground's top face; with Physics.queriesHitBackfaces off by default no hit is registered, so TryFindGroundBelow returns false and the prop is reported rather than repaired. Safe direction, but a capability the old 50 m ray had. Accept or add an explicit deep-recovery path.

findings.label: Downward moves are uncapped and unreported
findings.detail: The ray reaches height + 100 m downward and downward lifts are never capped or logged, so a prop sitting 50 m above the city is silently dropped to the road while a 1.1 m upward lift is refused and named. A silent bake is not evidence that nothing large moved. Consider reporting large downward moves too.

findings.label: Re-fit overwrites hand-tuned colliders
findings.detail: The already-knockable path now re-fits every non-reference box from the mesh, which is the intended repair for the 30 mis-oriented boxes but also discards any by-eye collider edit without a log line. Only the named reference object is protected. Costs nothing today since RoadBlocker04.002 is the only hand-fitted box.

findings.label: Brief's 1.985 m figure is wrong
findings.detail: For box dims (0.017257674, 0.004203821, 0.009454458) at uniform scale 230.0039 under quaternion (-0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5) the y row of localToWorldMatrix is (0, 0, 230.0039), so the vertical half-extent is 230.0039 * 0.009454458 / 2 = 1.087281 m. 1.985 m is half the local X extent, which this rotation sends to world -Z. The code, plan and proof all carry 1.087281 m and name the brief's error. The brief's identity figure of 0.4834 m is right and is the local-Y reading the old code used. Correct the brief so a later pass does not reverse the fix.

findings.label: Proof script quotes pre-fix axes for the lift caps
findings.detail: seat_math_check.py section 6 derives family heights from the mis-oriented boxes still in the scene, printing 'max(1 m, 9.21 m)' for a table whose post-fix height is 1.98 m and a 3.31 m cap for a bin that is 2.57 m. Both conclusions survive (1.02 < 1.98, 6.24 > 2.57) but the quoted caps are not what the shipped C# computes. Fix: derive them from the corrected box.

findings.label: Headline wording understates the re-fit
findings.detail: The summary still says the already-knockable props 'were re-seated on the road in place', which no longer describes the work now that their boxes are re-fitted as well.

findings.label: Rotation-mismatch warning names one prop
findings.detail: The warning in ApplyReferenceBox is keyed by reference.name through rotationWarned, so the first off-angle prop is named and the rest are silent, where the unseated list names every offender.

findings.label: WorldExtents reports a world AABB
findings.detail: WorldExtents returns the world-aligned bounding box of the rotated collider, which equals the box's own dimensions only for 90-degree multiples. Correct for all four current families, but it will overstate a tilted prop's size and can trip the < 0.1 m or > 6 m self-check lists when lamps and signs are added.

findings.label: Change is uncommitted
findings.detail: KnockablePropBaker.cs is modified in the working tree and docs/tooling/seat_math_check.py and docs/tooling/seat-fix-plan.md are untracked; the plan's final step (one commit on fix/seat-on-road-rotation, three files added by name) has not run.
